svg.title: One public URL, independent regional origins
svg.desc: Optional manually configured Azure Front Door forwards the unchanged Microsoft caller token to either regional Function. Each origin retains Easy Auth, local identities, storage, a vault with the same decryption key, and telemetry. Dashed lines represent separate non-delivering readiness probes requiring custom code. Live calls use the same selected provider; this is not provider fallback.
svg.text: One public URL, independent regional origins
Original design illustration. Optional manual setup, not a shipped deployment.
Microsoft Entra ID
One endpoint app and public encryption certificate
Azure Front Door: one public /api/SendOtp URL
Route by health, priority, latency and weight; no fixed traffic split.
Forward the original bearer token and encrypted body unchanged.
Region A
Function + Easy Auth
Same issuer, audience and caller policy
Validate / decrypt; evaluate or send
Local Key Vault, storage and identities
Matching private key; local vault reference
Local telemetry and provider authorization
Separate readiness handler
Key usable; no provider call or message
Region B
Function + Easy Auth
Same issuer, audience and caller policy
Validate / decrypt; evaluate or send
Local Key Vault, storage and identities
Matching private key; local vault reference
Local telemetry and provider authorization
Separate readiness handler
Key usable; no provider call or message
Live calls only
Same selected phone provider
Regional failover does not provide provider fallback.
Responses return through Front Door. Live success is acceptance, not handset receipt.
Dashed: HEAD /api/health/ready probes. This handler is not included in release packages.
Restrict both origins to this Front Door profile; keep Easy Auth on SendOtp.
Each region needs the full peak workload capacity and independently usable dependencies.
